The 4th paragraph begins 'In the phonological inventory, as sketched out in Anonby and Mohebbi Bahmani, Kholosi has retained elements of the retroflexed (or postalveolar) series well-known from Indic languages (see Cardona and Jain..)' and ends exactly: 'Other salient phonological phenomena are pervasive vowel nasalization, likely the allophonic realization of word-final n post-vocalically, and pitch accent rather than stress or lexical tone as the basis of the prosodic system.' The reported quote is verb…
new_statements.rule_in_words: The describers characterise Kholosi word prosody as a pitch accent system, explicitly not a stress system and not lexical tone. They do not say which syllable carries the accent. The only open elaboration (Arora 2020 ms, sec. 2.3.2, following Anonby & Mohebbi Bahmani 2016) says pitch is demarcative for words/syllables rather than lexically contrastive, that non-final long-vowel syllables tend to take low pitch with a HL fall on the final syllable (e.g. šor.ko L.HL, pe.ter H.HL, pa.ro.no HL.L.HL), and that numerals carry high pitch on the first syllable falling through the word; no general placement rule is stated anywhere I could open.
new_statements.exceptions: None in the Iranica entry. Arora 2020 notes a possible link between morphological class and pitch pattern (numerals initial-High) attributed to Anonby, and length-conditioned low pitch on non-final long vowels.
new_statements.domain_note: Statement is about the word-level prosodic system in general ('the basis of the prosodic system'); based on elicited lexical items (Anonby & Mohebbi Bahmani wordlist fieldwork) rather than connected speech. Two-page encyclopaedia entry written by the primary fieldworkers, summarising Anonby & Mohebbi Bahmani 2016 and later field notes; it is first-hand but not the full description.
new_statements.identity_note: All sources describe the same variety: Kholosi (xolosi) of the villages Kholos (Ḵoloṣ) and Gotāv, Bastak district, western Hormozgan = Glottolog khol1241 (no ISO 639-3 code in Glottolog 5.1; a UniMorph repo uses 'hsi'). Arora's data come from one speaker from Kholos (Ahmed Etebari); Anonby & Mohebbi Bahmani's from wordlist elicitation in Kholos. Note the Iranica page gives Vol. XVI Fasc. 5 pp. 561-562 and online date 14 Dec 2020, whereas the langsci-395 bibliography cites it as 2019, pp. 541-542.

sources.note: Sec. 2.3.2 'Pitch accent' (p.10): 'As in Anonby and Bahmani [2016], I found strong evidence that pitch is important for word and syllable demarcation, if not lexically contrastive. Vowel length also is tied to pitch; non-final syllables with long vowel nuclei tend to take a low pitch.. numerals, which all bear high pitch on the first syllable which progressively falls over the word.' Pitch contours given per word (H.HL, L.HL etc.); no general placement rule; the word 'stress' is not used for Kholosi.
